label: rejected

evidence.V1: Front, three-quarter and silhouette all read as a splayed grass tuft and the top view is a clear radial star, so it is readable from every angle.
evidence.V2: About 11 blades of near-identical width and length. The only variation is a tip/base two-tone, with no short filler blades and no ground tuft, so the hierarchy is only partial.
evidence.V3: Curved, tapered blades give some stylised gesture, but they are uniform in width and the bases end as abrupt flat-cut stubs at different heights (silhouette shows a notched, ragged base).
evidence.V4: Blades have sharp knife-edge tips and hard cut-off bottoms. There is no soft rounding where blades fuse into a clump, so edge treatment is inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Close base studio shows visible stray faceting: kinked segment bands along each blade, hard shading breaks at the segment joins, and ragged, separate-shell blade bottoms (62 cross-shell overlaps) instead of a fused base.
evidence.V6: One foliage-green hue in about 3 values (dark base, mid body, light tip). Colourways (autumn, frost) keep the same disciplined structure.
evidence.V7: 528 tris against a small-class target of 600 (ceiling 1500), so it is under target.
evidence.V8: Correct single LF_VertexColor material and palette discipline, but the blades are separate, faceted segmented shells rather than the kit's fused smooth organic shell.
evidence.V9: Studio line: foliage Anchored, CanCollide/CanTouch/CanQuery off, Box fidelity, Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre. Correct.

artifacts: stray faceting / segment kinks along blades with hard shading bands
ragged flat-cut blade bottoms at differing heights instead of a fused root mass
top_fixes: Fuse the blade roots into one smooth clump base that sits flush on the ground plane
Add more segments or weighted normals along the blade curve to remove the kinked faceting
Vary blade length and width (add a few short filler blades) for big/medium/small hierarchy
